source_refs.note: Inheritance of Human Skin Colour: a main subheading of 18.5.1 Polygenic Inheritance, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 97-98.

blocks.text: Skin colour depends on the amount of melanin pigment. More melanin means darker skin; less melanin means lighter skin. This trait is controlled by polygenes (about 60 genes), but for understanding, we take 3 genes: A, B, C. Each of these genes has a dominant and a recessive allele.

items: Alleles A, B, and C produce more melanin
Alleles a, b, and c produce less melanin

blocks.text: If the parents have genotypes AABBCC (very dark) and aabbcc (very light), all of their children will be AaBbCc (intermediate colour). If both parents are triple heterozygotes i.e., AaBbCc, their children will have wide range of skin colours from very dark to very light. The ratio of different skin colours will be 1 : 6 : 15 : 20 : 15 : 6 : 1 (from very dark to very light).

blocks.alt: Upper panel: parents dark red wheat AABBCC x white wheat aabbcc; gametes ABC and abc; F1 AaBbCc, intermediate red wheat. Lower panel: AaBbCc x AaBbCc, each forming eight kinds of gametes (ABC, AbC, ABc, Abc, aBC, abC, aBc, abc), combined in an 8 x 8 grid of 64 genotypes, each cell shaded from dark red to white by the number of dominant alleles. Below: 63 Red (various shades) : 1 White, and a row of seven classes with their counts.
